scope: Source-table transcription and an explicitly truncated para-H2 level calculation; not the full original cooling curve.

Equation (7), J=2 spontaneous decay rate in s^-1
J=2 to 0 photon energy in erg
Recursion agrees with independent constrained rate-matrix solution
Net collisional energy loss equals emitted radiative energy

external_reference_comparison.interpretation: A finite-ladder comparison, not a validated reproduction of every Table 2 entry. The largest discrepancy is retained openly, without fitting or replacing missing coefficients.

limitations: Only para-H2, H-atom collisions, adjacent even-J transitions, and spontaneous downward emission.
Steady, optically thin populations at fixed gas temperature and H-atom density; no thermal or chemical equilibrium of the gas is solved.
The finite ladder varies with available Table 1 entries: maximum J=2,4,6,or8. No missing upward rate is invented or interpolated.
Historical rounded energy and detailed-balance prefactors are preserved separately; no modern H2 rates are substituted.
The source warns that the high-temperature calculation is less reliable and only estimates low-temperature accuracy; implementation checks do not validate the atomic data.
Table 1 upward rates are distinct from the downward rates derived with equation (9).
Table 2 is an external comparison, not an assertion that the truncated Table 1 model reproduces every entry.
The source coefficient accuracy is not independently assessed. Its discussion on p. 83 warns about the potential approximation and high-temperature accuracy.
The origin of discrepancies, including the 200 K high-density entry, requires additional level/rate information or a source erratum; no correction is invented.
